Afghanistan / China.note: Settled by the 1963 treaty along the 1895 Wakhan line.

Afghanistan / Iran.note: Persia–Afghanistan line, settled by the McMahon award of 1905.

Afghanistan / Pakistan.note: The Durand Line, British India's border with Afghanistan from 1893.

Afghanistan / Uzbekistan.note: The Amu Darya, Russo-British agreements of 1873–95.

Albania / Kosovo.note: Albania against Yugoslavia; Italian Albania took most of Kosovo 1941–44.

Algeria / Libya.note: Ghadames line of 1919; the south was settled in 1956.

Algeria / Mali.note: Algeria's southern line against French West Africa, on maps by the 1940s.

Algeria / Mauritania.note: Algeria's southern line against French West Africa, on maps by the 1940s.

Algeria / Morocco.note: Drawn from the French protectorate on; the south was approximate until the 1972 treaty.

Algeria / Niger.note: Algeria's southern line against French West Africa, on maps by the 1940s.

Algeria / Tunisia.note: The southern end was disputed until the 1970 agreement.

Algeria / W. Sahara.note: Spanish Sahara against French Algeria, drawn once Spain held the interior.

Angola / Congo.note: Cabinda against French Congo, Franco-Portuguese convention of 1886.

Angola / Dem. Rep. Congo.note: Settled once the Dilolo exchange of 1927 took effect.

Armenia / Azerbaijan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Armenia / Georgia.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Austria / Czechia.note: Bohemia and Moravia against Austria; inside Germany from the Munich Agreement to 1945.

Austria / Germany.note: Austria against Bavaria since Salzburg went to Austria in 1816; gone during the Anschluss.

Austria / Hungary.note: Final once Burgenland joined Austria in 1921.

Austria / Italy.note: Saint-Germain line through the Tyrol, from 1920.

Austria / Liechtenstein.note: Liechtenstein against Austria; Germany during the Anschluss.

Austria / Slovakia.note: Austria against Czechoslovakia along the Morava, from the 1920 treaties.

Austria / Switzerland.note: Vorarlberg and Tyrol against Switzerland since 1815.

Azerbaijan / Georgia.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Azerbaijan / Iran.note: The Aras line of the Treaty of Turkmenchay, 1828.

Azerbaijan / Russia.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Azerbaijan / Turkey.note: Turkey's short border with Nakhchivan came with the 1932 Turkey–Iran exchange.

Belarus / Latvia.note: A Soviet republic line until Latvia's return to independence.

Belarus / Lithuania.note: A Soviet republic line until Lithuania's return to independence.

Belarus / Russia.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Belarus / Ukraine.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Belgium / Germany.note: Eupen-Malmedy went to Belgium in 1920; annexed by Germany 1940–44.

Benin / Burkina Faso.note: Upper Volta was split up 1932–47; this line dates from its return.

Benin / Niger.note: Dahomey against the colony of Niger, along the Niger river.

Benin / Togo.note: Dahomey against German Togo, 1897; the same line under French Togo.

Bhutan / China.note: The traditional line, held de facto since 1959; never formally agreed.

Bhutan / India.note: Bhutan against British India after the Duars War of 1865.

Bosnia and Herz. / Croatia.note: Inside Yugoslavia until Bosnia was recognised in 1992.

Bosnia and Herz. / Montenegro.note: Inside Yugoslavia until Bosnia was recognised in 1992.

Bosnia and Herz. / Serbia.note: Inside Yugoslavia until Bosnia was recognised in 1992.

Botswana / Zambia.note: The Kazungula meeting point on the Zambezi.

Brazil / France.note: French Guiana's southern line, Swiss award of 1900.

Brunei / Malaysia.note: Brunei's line after Limbang went to Sarawak in 1890.

Bulgaria / Greece.note: Fixed once Western Thrace was Greek, confirmed at Lausanne in 1923.

Bulgaria / Macedonia.note: Bulgaria against Yugoslavia; Bulgaria held Vardar Macedonia 1941–44.

Bulgaria / Romania.note: Southern Dobruja returned to Bulgaria in 1940.

Bulgaria / Serbia.note: The 1919 Neuilly line; changed in the 1941–44 occupation.

Bulgaria / Turkey.note: The Thracian line as confirmed at Lausanne in 1923.

Burkina Faso / Côte d'Ivoire.note: Upper Volta was split up 1932–47; this line dates from its return.

Burkina Faso / Ghana.note: The Gold Coast's northern boundary, Anglo-French convention of 1898.

Burkina Faso / Mali.note: Upper Volta was split up 1932–47; this line dates from its return.

Burkina Faso / Niger.note: Upper Volta was split up 1932–47; this line dates from its return.

Burkina Faso / Togo.note: Upper Volta was split up 1932–47; this line dates from its return.

Burundi / Dem. Rep. Congo.note: The Rusizi and Lake Tanganyika, German–Belgian agreement of 1910.

Burundi / Tanzania.note: Ruanda-Urundi against Tanganyika after the 1923–24 adjustments.

Cambodia / Thailand.note: The 1907 Franco-Siamese line; Thailand held the west 1941–46.

Cameroon / Central African Rep..note: Restored after the 1911–19 German Neukamerun cession.

Cameroon / Chad.note: Restored after the 1911–19 German Neukamerun cession.

Cameroon / Congo.note: Restored after the 1911–19 German Neukamerun cession.

Cameroon / Gabon.note: Restored after the 1911–19 German Neukamerun cession.

Canada / United States of America.note: Complete with the 1903 Alaska boundary award.

Central African Rep. / Chad.note: Inside French Equatorial Africa until independence; drawn loosely before.

Central African Rep. / Congo.note: Inside French Equatorial Africa until independence; drawn loosely before.

Central African Rep. / Dem. Rep. Congo.note: The Ubangi and Mbomu rivers, set between French Congo and the Congo Free State in 1887.

Central African Rep. / S. Sudan.note: Ubangi-Shari against the Sudan, demarcated by 1924.

Central African Rep. / Sudan.note: Ubangi-Shari against the Sudan, demarcated by 1924.

Chad / Libya.note: The 1919 line most maps kept; the Aouzou Strip was disputed until 1994.

Chad / Niger.note: Fixed once Tibesti moved to Chad in 1929–30.

Chad / Sudan.note: Wadai against Darfur, agreed 1919 and demarcated by 1924.

China / India.note: The line of actual control after the 1962 war; drawn variously before and still disputed.

China / Laos.note: French Indochina against China, convention of 1895.

China / Myanmar.note: Settled by the 1960 treaty; the north was undefined before.

China / North Korea.note: The Yalu and Tumen, settled with the Gando convention of 1909.

China / Pakistan.note: Settled by the 1963 agreement; British India's line with China was undefined here.

China / Russia.note: The Amur and Ussuri, Convention of Peking, 1860.

Congo / Gabon.note: Final when the Haut-Ogooué went back to Gabon in 1946.

Croatia / Hungary.note: The Trianon line; Hungary held Međimurje 1941–45.

Croatia / Montenegro.note: Inside Yugoslavia until Croatia was recognised in 1992.

Croatia / Serbia.note: Inside Yugoslavia until Croatia was recognised in 1992.

Croatia / Slovenia.note: Inside Yugoslavia until both were recognised in 1992.

Czechia / Germany.note: The Bohemian border with Saxony and Bavaria; the Sudetenland was German 1938–45.

Czechia / Poland.note: Czechoslovakia against Poland once Silesia became Polish in 1945.

Czechia / Slovakia.note: International only while Slovakia was separate, 1939–45, and since 1993.

Côte d'Ivoire / Ghana.note: Gold Coast against Ivory Coast, Anglo-French agreement of 1905.

Côte d'Ivoire / Mali.note: Redrawn when Upper Volta was split up in 1932 and put back in 1947.

Dem. Rep. Congo / Rwanda.note: Lake Kivu line, German–Belgian agreement of 1910.

Dem. Rep. Congo / S. Sudan.note: Settled once the Lado Enclave went to the Sudan in 1910.

Dem. Rep. Congo / Zambia.note: Congo Free State against British Central Africa, 1894.

Djibouti / Ethiopia.note: French Somaliland and Ethiopia, Franco-Ethiopian treaty of 1897.

Djibouti / Somaliland.note: French and British Somaliland, Anglo-French agreement of 1888.

Egypt / Israel.note: The 1906 Sinai line, also drawn while Israel held Sinai.

Egypt / Sudan.note: The 22nd parallel of the 1899 condominium agreement.

Eq. Guinea / Gabon.note: Rio Muni against French Congo, Franco-Spanish treaty of 1900.

Eritrea / Ethiopia.note: Gone inside Italian East Africa (1936–41) and after Ethiopia annexed Eritrea (1962–93).

Estonia / Latvia.note: Between the Baltic states, gone while they were Soviet.

Estonia / Russia.note: Today's line dates from Estonia's return to independence; the 1920–40 line ran further east.

Ethiopia / Kenya.note: Anglo-Ethiopian treaty of 1907; later adjustments don't show at globe scale.

Ethiopia / Somalia.note: The provisional administrative line from the 1950 trust territory on.

Ethiopia / Somaliland.note: British Somaliland and Ethiopia, Anglo-Ethiopian treaty of 1897.

Finland / Russia.note: The armistice of 1944, which took Karelia and Petsamo.

France / Germany.note: The Rhine and Lorraine line; moved west while Alsace-Lorraine was German (1871–1918, 1940–44).

France / Italy.note: From the cession of Nice and Savoy; the 1947 changes don't show at this scale.

France / Luxembourg.note: Luxembourg against France since the 1839 settlement.

France / Switzerland.note: Complete once Savoy went to France in 1860.

Georgia / Russia.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Germany / Luxembourg.note: Luxembourg against Prussia, then Germany; annexed 1940–44.

Germany / Netherlands.note: The 1815 line; small post-war rectifications don't show at this scale.

Germany / Poland.note: The Oder–Neisse line, from Potsdam in 1945.

Germany / Switzerland.note: The Rhine and Lake Constance line, unchanged since 1815.

Ghana / Togo.note: The British and French Togoland line of 1919–20, Ghana's since 1957.

Greece / Turkey.note: The Evros line, Treaty of Lausanne, 1923.

Guyana / Suriname.note: The Courantyne; the New River Triangle is disputed.

Guyana / Venezuela.note: The 1899 Paris award, disputed by Venezuela since 1962.

Hungary / Romania.note: The Trianon line; Hungary held northern Transylvania 1940–44.

Hungary / Serbia.note: The Trianon line; Hungary held Bačka 1941–44.

Hungary / Slovakia.note: The Trianon line; Hungary held southern Slovakia 1938–45.

Hungary / Slovenia.note: The Trianon line; Hungary held Prekmurje 1941–45.

Hungary / Ukraine.note: The Czechoslovak–Hungarian line of 1920, Soviet from 1945.

India / Myanmar.note: Burma was separated from India in 1937.

India / Nepal.note: Nepal against British India, final with the 1860 return of the Terai.

Indonesia / Timor-Leste.note: The 1914 line; gone while Indonesia held East Timor.

Iran / Iraq.note: Constantinople protocol of 1913–14; the Shatt al-Arab changes don't show at this scale.

Iran / Pakistan.note: Persia against British Baluchistan, demarcated by 1896.

Iraq / Kuwait.note: Agreed in 1923; erased during the 1990–91 annexation.

Iraq / Saudi Arabia.note: The Uqair line of 1922 with a Neutral Zone between, divided in 1981; drawn dashed on globes before.

Iraq / Syria.note: Fixed by the League of Nations in 1932.

Israel / Jordan.note: Transjordan's line with Palestine along the Jordan valley and the Arava.

Israel / Syria.note: The 1923 line, with the Golan shown as Syrian.

Italy / San Marino.note: San Marino's border, unchanged for centuries.

Italy / Slovenia.note: Final after the Free Territory of Trieste was divided in 1954.

Italy / Switzerland.note: Ticino and Graubünden against Lombardy and Piedmont, then Italy.

Jordan / Palestine.note: The Jordan river; the West Bank was Jordanian 1950–67.

Jordan / Saudi Arabia.note: The 1965 land swap that gave Jordan more of the Aqaba coast.

Kazakhstan / Kyrgyzstan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Kazakhstan / Russia.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Kazakhstan / Turkmenistan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Kazakhstan / Uzbekistan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Kenya / S. Sudan.note: The 1914 Kenya–Sudan line, with the Ilemi Triangle shown on the Kenyan side.

Kenya / Somalia.note: Jubaland went from Kenya to Italian Somaliland in 1925.

Kenya / Uganda.note: Final after Uganda's Rudolf Province went to Kenya in 1926.

Kosovo / Macedonia.note: Macedonia against Serbia from Macedonia's admission in 1993.

Kosovo / Serbia.note: Kosovo's declaration of 2008, shown on most maps since.

Kuwait / Saudi Arabia.note: The Neutral Zone was divided in 1969.

Kyrgyzstan / Tajikistan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Kyrgyzstan / Uzbekistan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Laos / Thailand.note: The Mekong and the 1904–07 lines; Thailand held the west bank 1941–46.

Latvia / Lithuania.note: Between the Baltic states, gone while they were Soviet.

Latvia / Russia.note: Today's line dates from Latvia's return to independence; the 1920–40 line included Abrene.

Lesotho / South Africa.note: Basutoland's border, Treaty of Aliwal North, 1869.

Libya / Sudan.note: Settled when the Sarra Triangle went to Italian Libya in 1934.

Lithuania / Russia.note: Lithuania against Kaliningrad, from Lithuania's return to independence.

Macedonia / Serbia.note: Inside Yugoslavia until Macedonia's admission in 1993.

Mali / Mauritania.note: The Hodh went from French Sudan to Mauritania in 1944.

Mali / Niger.note: Redrawn when Upper Volta was split up in 1932 and put back in 1947.

Mali / Senegal.note: French Sudan against Senegal; inside the Mali Federation 1959–60.

Mauritania / Senegal.note: The Senegal river, from Mauritania's founding as a colony.

Moldova / Romania.note: The Prut; Bessarabia was Romanian 1918–40 and 1941–44.

Moldova / Ukraine.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Mongolia / Russia.note: Final once Tuva joined the Soviet Union in 1944.

Morocco / W. Sahara.note: The 27°40′ line of the 1912 Franco-Spanish convention.

Mozambique / South Africa.note: Delagoa Bay award of 1875 and the earlier Transvaal line.

Mozambique / Tanzania.note: The Rovuma, final once the Kionga Triangle went to Mozambique in 1919.

Namibia / South Africa.note: The Orange river, Anglo-German agreement of 1890.

Namibia / Zambia.note: The Caprivi Strip, Anglo-German agreement of 1890.

North Korea / South Korea.note: The 1953 armistice line. Before it Korea was one country, divided on the 38th parallel from 1945 (an old line).

Norway / Sweden.note: Drawn between the two kingdoms throughout their union.

Oman / Saudi Arabia.note: Settled by the 1990 treaty; approximate before.

Oman / Yemen.note: Settled by the 1992 treaty; approximate before.

Poland / Ukraine.note: The Soviet–Polish line of 1945; the 1951 exchange doesn't show at this scale.

Portugal / Spain.note: Unchanged since Olivenza went to Spain in 1801.

Qatar / Saudi Arabia.note: Agreed in 1965 and demarcated in 1999; approximate before.

Romania / Ukraine.note: The Soviet–Romanian line from the 1944 armistice.

Russia / Ukraine.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Rwanda / Tanzania.note: Ruanda-Urundi against Tanganyika after the 1923–24 adjustments.

Saudi Arabia / United Arab Emirates.note: Settled by the 1974 Jeddah treaty, after the Buraimi dispute; approximate before.

Saudi Arabia / Yemen.note: Settled by the 2000 Jeddah treaty; the 1934 Taif line covered only the west.

Slovakia / Ukraine.note: Czechoslovakia ceded Carpathian Ruthenia to the Soviet Union in 1945.

Somalia / Somaliland.note: British against Italian Somaliland until they united in 1960. Most maps show one Somalia since.

Syria / Turkey.note: Final when Hatay joined Turkey in 1939.

Tajikistan / Uzbekistan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.

Turkmenistan / Uzbekistan.note: A Soviet republic line until the Soviet Union ended.
